query: Our payment API runs Node.js 16 from nodejs/node. Is it acceptable to keep this runtime in production, or should we upgrade?
answer:
Target:   nodejs/node @ 07b0481 · node@16.20.2 · checked 2026-11-21
Decision: 🔴 Do not adopt

Do not keep Node.js 16 in production for a payment API; plan an upgrade to a supported LTS release
soon. The scan shows eight known vulnerabilities including a critical one. Node 16's support end was
not confirmed by the tools, so verify it on the official release schedule.

Why
 🟢 Licence: Permissive MIT-style licence text; GitHub reports no standard SPDX id.
   • LICENSE:6 The licence is a permissive, MIT-style licence, so commercial use is allowed. GitHub
     shows no standard id because the file also bundles other notices.
     "Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy" → https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/07b0481f495415cca2e12a4b5b52cddbe00556b4/LICENSE#L6 ✔
 🔴 Security: Eight known CVEs listed for 16.20.2, including one rated critical (9.8). (CRA Art.
   13(5))
   • Version 16.20.2 has a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-111497).
     "A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through" → https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-111497 ✔
   • Node.js 16.20.2 is linked to several known vulnerabilities, including a critical one (score
     9.8) in the bundled Brotli decompression code. For a payment API this is a serious risk.
     "A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through" → https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-111497 ✔
   🔴 16.20.2: critical vulnerability CVE-2026-111497

What to do next
 1. Plan an upgrade of the payment API to a currently supported Node.js LTS (long-term support)
   release, and test it first in a staging environment.
 2. Until then, confirm on nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases that Node 16 gets no more security
   fixes, and treat any unpatched critical issues as open risk.
 3. Reduce exposure meanwhile: keep the API behind a firewall or gateway, and avoid decoding
   untrusted Brotli-compressed input.

Limitations
 • Open question: Which exact Node.js 16.x version is deployed?
 • Open question: Is the API reachable from the public internet, and does it accept Brotli-
   compressed requests?

Also checked: maintenance 🟡 Main repo is active, but Node 16 line… · Not checked: privacy, skills
